subject: strIndexVsCall
why: E5e1 `int(s[i]) + m()` (s = "ab", i captured; m: i = 1, returns 5): the byte read s[i] is a bounds-checked pure op on the string VALUE (spec#Index_expressions), spec-unsequenced against m — before m 'a' 97 + 5 = 102, after m 'b' 98 + 5 = 103 (gc's, 20/20 under GOMAXPROCS 1/8, default and -N -l: the plain byte read deferred after the call — where str-slice-vs-call's string SLICE is hoisted before it); the ONE consumption site is the `unseq` scheduler's pick (`unseqNext`, bound = the ready-set size at each pick; Stage E5 E5e, 2026-09-22 — design docs/2026-09-22_unseq-stage-e5-design.md §E5e). members=2

subject: strIndexPanicVsPrint
expected_reason: index out of range [9] with length 2
why: E5e4 `int(s[i]) + wit(5)` (s = "ab", i = 9 a private local; wit prints `wit 5`): the byte read's bounds check FAILS, spec-unsequenced against the printing call — the panic before wit (no output) or after it (`wit 5` printed — gc's, call-first): the E13 sibling-panic shape on a string byte read; a status-diverse single row (ok vs panic) is refused by the membership lane by name unless it declares a status set (audit F8's mechanism, unused in the corpus — not taken here), hence this panic/panic row beside the ok/ok one; the ONE consumption site is the `unseq` scheduler's pick (`unseqNext`, bound = the ready-set size at each pick; Stage E5 E5e, 2026-09-22 — design docs/2026-09-22_unseq-stage-e5-design.md §E5e). members=2

subject: strSliceVsCall
why: E5e2 `int(s[i:][0]) + m()` (s = "ab", i captured; m: i = 1, returns 5): the substring s[i:] is a bounds-checked pure op on the string VALUE and its byte [0] a second, both spec-unsequenced against m — before m 'a' 97 + 5 = 102 (gc's — 20/20 draws under GOMAXPROCS 1/8, default and -N -l: order.go hoists the string slice's temporary before the call, where the plain byte read of str-index-vs-call is deferred after it), after m 'b' 98 + 5 = 103; `len(s[i:]) + m()` would be all-forced (the substring inside len's window, len before m — the strict control's shape); the ONE consumption site is the `unseq` scheduler's pick (`unseqNext`, bound = the ready-set size at each pick; Stage E5 E5e, 2026-09-22 — design docs/2026-09-22_unseq-stage-e5-design.md §E5e). members=2
